hooks.text: A giant comet once hid in plain daylight.
Why did the world ignore a comet visible at noon?
The brightest comet of the century was a media secret.

title: The Great Comet the World Ignored
description: Comet West was one of the brightest visitors from the Oort Cloud, but a previous space dud kept it out of the headlines.

beats.text: A giant comet once hid in plain daylight.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a bright comet near the Sun in a blue daylight sky

beats.text: It outshone the stars, but the media stayed silent.
beats.visual: photograph of Comet West in the dawn sky showing a bright head and tail, 1976

beats.text: Reporters were still embarrassed by a previous space dud.
beats.visual: photograph of Comet Kohoutek taken from the Skylab space station, 1974

beats.text: When Richard West spotted this one, newsrooms ignored him.
beats.visual: photograph of astronomer Richard M. West at the European Southern Observatory
queries: ESO La Silla Observatory Schmidt telescope

beats.text: As the icy visitor rounded the Sun, something snapped.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a comet nucleus glowing intensely as it approaches the Sun

beats.text: Extreme gravity tore the comet into four distinct pieces.
beats.visual: illustration of a comet nucleus breaking into four fragments labeled A, B, C, and D

beats.text: These shards released a massive fan of glowing dust.
beats.visual: wide shot photograph of Comet West's fan-shaped dust tail in 1976

beats.text: It painted a tail across thirty degrees of the sky.
beats.visual: long exposure of Comet West showing synchronic bands in the broad tail

beats.text: It was the greatest show that nearly stayed hidden in daylight.
beats.visual: photograph of the bright head of Comet West in the dawn sky over a landscape

better_than_last: I shortened beat 1 to exactly 8 words to strictly meet the length limit while maintaining maximum impact for early audience retention.
